A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ForceVLA work. Their complete main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–E are available and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original real-world robotic experiments across five manipulation tasks, generalization tests, and fusion ablations in Section 5, plus router analysis and multi-task results in Appendices C–D.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experimental results, including Figure 5, Tables 1–3 and 5, and the appendix analyses and visual demonstrations.

M1.justification: Sections 3–4 and Table 4 retain the same force projection, four-expert top-1 FVLMoE fusion, and conditioning of the flow-based action head. No algorithm, architecture, or inference procedure changes.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same five-task ForceVLA-Data collection, object and height variations, visual occlusion and unstable-socket scenarios, and four-task joint evaluation in Appendix D.

E2.justification: Figure 5 and Tables 2 and 5 retain the same π0-base and π0-fast variants with and without force. Table 3 also retains the same early- and late-fusion comparators.

E3.justification: Training budgets, preprocessing, metrics, and evaluation procedures are unchanged. Section 5.1 retains 20 trials for insertion and pumping, 10 for wiping, and 15 cucumber-peeling trials; Appendix B retains the same training settings.

E4.justification: The fusion ablations, generalization and robustness tests, trajectory case studies, Appendix C router analysis, and Appendix E visual demonstrations are all retained without changes to their questions or evidence.

E5.justification: Appendix C retains the same averaging of routing probabilities across approximately 10 episodes per task. Neither version adds or revises seed information, uncertainty intervals, error bars, or statistical significance tests.

E6.justification: Numerical results and qualitative findings are unchanged throughout the main text and appendices. ForceVLA retains the 60.5% main-task average in Figure 5, 63.78% generalization average in Table 2, and 67.5% multi-task average in Table 5.

T1.justification: The policy formulation, sparse expert-routing expression, and token-fusion equations in Sections 3–4 are unchanged. No mathematical definitions, assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: force-aware FVLMoE fusion, ForceVLA-Data, and improved manipulation success and generalization. Their scientific scope and performance claims are unchanged.

C2.justification: Both versions retain the same explanations of force fusion, disruption from early fusion, and expert specialization. The limitations concerning estimated wrench precision and reliance on costly force-sensing platforms also remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Section 4.3, Appendices A–B, and Table 4 retain identical collection, preprocessing, hardware, optimizer, dimensionality, and training-time details. Both PDFs promise code and data release through the same project hyperlink.

R1.justification: Section 2 and all 51 references are unchanged, as is the positioning relative to VLA models, contact-rich manipulation methods, and mixture-of-experts research.

P1.justification: The author block changes Qiaojun Yu from an equal-contribution designation to the corresponding-author designation, removes the other corresponding-author markers, and replaces the contact email. The version/date header changes; scientific prose and section organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Minor spacing and reflow move one introduction line from page 2 to page 1, with small bibliography spacing shifts. Figures 1–19 and Tables 1–5 retain their content, structure, captions, and placement.

improvement.justification: v2 updates author and correspondence information and makes minor layout adjustments while retaining the scientific content and supporting evidence, including all appendices. These changes do not materially alter the paper's rigor, reproducibility, completeness, or readability.
